messages.subject: Syntax suggestions... empirical distribution
parts:
I'm looking for either tool or syntax suggestions. I have a dataset
which is organized as:

Patient Event Time
...
...

Let's say I have 100 observations that have events. (While normally I
might see these data transformed into a hazard function, we
don't have observation intervals for non-events, so no reliable
denominator. ) What I need is a graph of the instantaneous % of the
total event count, and a cumulative rate for each value of Time where
I have an event.

Each patient has only one event. Many patients never have an event and
their Time = .

For each value of Time, I need to estimate both the instantaneous
percentage of all events that occur and the cumulative percentage of
events that have occurred, so that eventually, I get something like:

Time Events Inst_Rate Cum_Rate
0 0 0 0 <- /* This row might be
hard to produce, so it is illustrative, not required */
1 5 5/100 5/100
2 5 5/95 10/100
3 90 90/90 100/100

(obviously, I'm looking for the real value of the fractions, not the
fractions...)

I'm trying to imagine a way to do this in stat_summary, or even outside
of ggplot. But I can't see how to end stat_summary to this purpose, and
I can't see how to bend reshape either. Suggestions welcome.

Eventually I'll have multiple rates, one for each level of a classifying
vector, but I first need to break the back on this
